title: Rust: Concurrency Basics
description: Spawn threads and use concurrency primitives in Rust.

steps.title: Spawn a Thread
steps.description: Use `std::thread::spawn` to create a thread that prints `"Hello from a thread!"`. Wait for it with `.join()`. Print `"Main thread done"` after.
hints: `let handle = std::thread::spawn(|| { println!("Hello from a thread!"); });`
The closure runs in a separate OS thread.

verification.failureMessage: Spawn a thread, print from it, and wait for it to finish.

steps.title: Multiple Threads
steps.description: Spawn 5 threads, each printing `"Thread N"` where N is its number. Join all handles and print `"All threads done"`.
hints: Use a `for` loop to spawn threads.

verification.failureMessage: Spawn 5 threads and print from each.

steps.title: Return Values from Threads
steps.description: Spawn a thread that computes `1 + 2 + ... + 100` and returns the result. Capture the return value from `.join()` and print it.
hints: The closure can return a value: `thread::spawn(move || { 42 })`.

verification.failureMessage: Compute 1..100 sum in a thread and print 5050.

steps.title: move Closures
steps.description: Create a `String` in main, then spawn a thread that prints it using `move`. Verify the move is needed (try to use the string after the move in comments).
hints: The `move` keyword transfers ownership to the thread.

verification.failureMessage: Move a String into a thread and print it.

steps.title: Scoped Threads (crossbeam-free)
steps.description: Use `thread::scope` to spawn threads that borrow local variables without `move`. Spawn two threads that each print part of a shared Vec.
hints: Scoped threads allow borrowing (no move needed).
The scope waits for all threads to finish.

verification.failureMessage: Use thread::scope to borrow a Vec in spawned threads.
